title: Lamport and vector clocks
summary: Implement Lamport clocks for a causality-respecting order and vector clocks that can tell "happened before" from "concurrent".

complexity.time: O(n) for the copy, n = processes
complexity.space: O(n) per process and per message

hints: Both clocks follow one rule: every event (local, send or receive) advances your own counter, and a receive must land after the send it answers. A Lamport clock is that rule with one integer; a vector clock keeps one integer per process.

Lamport receive: max(local, received) + 1. Vector receive: take the element-wise max of the two vectors, then add 1 to your own entry only. Return copies of vectors so a message can't change after it is sent.
compare(a, b): compute whether a <= b in every position and whether b <= a in every position. Both means equal, only the first means before, only the second means after, neither means concurrent.
